meta.title: May Asks Chef Lucy
meta.textType: functional: an interview, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by May. On Friday, April ninth, the cooking course ended, and I interviewed Chef Lucy for our blog. We sat at a kitchen table in the community center. I put a small recorder next to her cup of tea. On the wall behind her hung a framed paper that said "Diploma." Teacher Kim read this post first, and then it went on the blog.

On Thursday, I wrote four questions in my notebook. First, I asked, "Who taught you to cook?" Next, I asked, "What did you study?" Then I asked, "Where did you work?" My last question came from Ravi, Leo's pen pal, "What should a beginner learn first?" Chef Lucy listened to each question and smiled.

Before the interview, a member of the center's staff took a photo of us. Chef Lucy, Lily, Mia, and I stood around a table of bowls in our aprons. The bowls were full of the sweet dish that we made. Chef Lucy has about twelve pupils in each course. The staff say that her course is always full. In the photo, everybody smiles, and the girls hold their bowls.

"I was taught to cook at home when I was nine," said Chef Lucy. "My grandmother's kitchen was my first classroom." "After school, I went to a college and studied cooking for two years." "My studies were hard, but I loved them." "I cooked every day, and I never stopped." "At the end, I was given a diploma." I looked at the framed paper on the wall. It was her diploma.

"Then I worked in a hotel kitchen for ten years," she said. "The cooks were given a room in the accommodation building of the hotel." "After that, I worked in a restaurant for five years." "The work was hard, and the days were long." "In those years, I gained a lot of experience." That was fifteen years in kitchens, and it was a long career.

"Ten years ago, this cooking school was opened," said Chef Lucy. "So I am a businesswoman, too." Her occupation is chef, and she is a teacher and a businesswoman. Then I read Ravi's question again. Chef Lucy thought for a moment. "Wash your hands and taste your food," she said. I smiled when I thought of her first classroom, a small kitchen at home. Thank you, Chef Lucy. Best wishes, May.
text.summary: May writes a blog post about her interview with Chef Lucy on the last morning of the cooking course. Chef Lucy tells where she learned to cook, where she studied and worked, and what a beginner should learn first.
